# Phase 01.1 Plan 14: SC5 Closure and Phase Reconciliation Summary

A 42-case discipline test proves the nineteen-file glyph migration finished, that no surface names a
raw ramp step, and that the SC5 residue table still enumerates all eleven requirement IDs — plus the
ROADMAP's SC5 drafting error corrected and the phase's four honest gaps written down instead of
carried.

## What was built

**Task 1 — `tests/theme/design-system-discipline.test.ts`** (commit `7d0c25a`, 42 cases).

Four assertion groups, each guarding a defect class no other test in the repo covers:

1. **The glyph migration is complete.** Walks all 81 `.ts`/`.tsx` files under `app/`, `components/`
   and `lib/`, extracts the value bindings each imports from the icon package, and asserts none is
   rendered as a bare JSX element. Nineteen files import glyphs; the migration was carried out by
   five different plans across three waves, and nothing until now asserted the last one landed.
2. **Ramp containment.** Asserts no file outside `app/tokens/cena.css` names a Cena ramp step.
3. **The SC5 residue is enumerated.** Parses the residue table out of `01.1-UI-SPEC.md`, asserts
   set-equality against the eleven requirement IDs the imported template self-declares, cross-checks
   the table against the prose tally immediately above it, and asserts each partial row names an
   owning phase.
4. **The three diner copy groups SC5 names by function** exist in all of `hu`/`en`/`ro`.

**Task 3 — reconciliation** (commit `59c6869`). ROADMAP SC5 reworded; `.design-sync/NOTES.md` given
a phase close-out section.

**Task 2 — the design-project write-back was NOT performed by this executor.** See below.

## Task 2: reassigned to the orchestrator, with a pre-flight I could do repo-side

Per the dispatch, `DesignSync` is unreachable from any subagent (established across three separate
dispatches in wave 1), so the write-back to cloud project `07b799d4-de60-4b17-8aec-106904d0b264` is
orchestrator-owned. I did not attempt it and produced no repo diff for it.

Repo-side preconditions verified green:

- `.planning/design-archive/readme-corrections.md` present (149 lines)
- `.planning/design-archive/readme-ORIGINAL.md` present (254 lines) and **unmodified** —
  `git diff` prints nothing, so the rollback path survives
- `git status --porcelain app components lib actions tests` prints nothing

### Three findings the orchestrator needs before applying the payload

**Finding A — the corrections doc's own provenance section is now stale, and it misinstructs.**
`readme-corrections.md` §"Provenance" states that `readme-ORIGINAL.md` "was NOT captured", that the
write-back is therefore "one-way, not costly", and that plan 01.1-14 "must capture `readme.md` to
`.planning/design-archive/readme-ORIGINAL.md` before it writes". **All three statements are now
false.** The archive exists, carries an `ARCHIVED VERBATIM … fetched 2026-08-05` provenance header,
and is byte-identical to the pre-edit source. The write-back is costly-but-reversible as the plan's
`reversibility` rating claims. I did not correct the doc — the plan declares it a read-only input and
it is absent from `files_modified`. **Recommendation:** strike that provenance block in a follow-up,
because as written it will send the next reader to re-capture a file that already exists, or worse,
to overwrite the archive with post-edit text and destroy the rollback copy.

**Finding B — the three "Current" blocks are paraphrases, and the live text is more scattered.** All
three are present in `readme-ORIGINAL.md`, but not in the single-block shape the corrections doc
quotes:

| Correction | Where it actually lives in the archived original |
|---|---|
| D-11 positioning | Lines 6–8, as the *second* sentence of paragraph 1. Paragraph 1 opens with a different sentence ("Cena is a restaurant operating system for independent restaurants — the thirty-to-eighty-seat places run by the people who own them.") that the Replacement does not mention. Applying the Replacement as a whole-paragraph swap would silently drop it. |
| D-04 lexicon rule | Lines 46–47. The live rule carries a trailing negative list the Replacement omits (`Never "records", "entities", "submit", "module", "resource"`). Dropping it removes the rule's software-words half. |
| D-04 four worked examples | **Not one block.** They occur at seven sites: the ✓/✕ table rows 67, 68, 69; the "Second person" bullet (44); the "Sentence case" bullet (49); and a JSX snippet (244, 245). Replacing "the four worked examples" as if they were contiguous leaves the banned lexicon standing at four of the seven. |
| W-3 currency rule | Lines 51–52, embedded mid-bullet ("Continental decimal comma for currency; 24-hour clock for service times") rather than as a standalone rule. The 24-hour-clock half must survive the replacement. |

**Finding C — task 2's lexicon acceptance criterion cannot be met by applying the payload verbatim,
and the conflict is real rather than a mis-grep.** The criterion requires the re-read lexicon section
to contain none of five service-tier words. After applying all three corrections, four sites in
§ Content fundamentals still carry them — and every one of them is a **voice-register demonstration**,
which D-04 says is kept *verbatim*:

- the errors bullet ("Printer in the pass is offline…")
- the empty-states bullet ("Nothing on the book yet for Tuesday…")
- the confirmations bullet ("Course fired to the pass. — Undo")
- the ✓/✕ table's first row ("Table 12 is 14 minutes past turn")

"Keep the register verbatim" and "the lexicon section contains none of these words" cannot both hold,
because the register is *demonstrated using the lexicon*. **Recommendation:** re-cut those four
demonstrations to menu-tier examples that preserve each one's shape exactly — same sentence
structure, same what-happened-then-what-to-do ordering, same past-tense-plus-undo — which honours
D-04's actual intent (the register is the *structure*, not the nouns) and satisfies the criterion.
That is a composition step, so it belongs to a human or the orchestrator, not to a mechanical apply.

Also unchanged and out of scope, per the payload's own "Explicitly NOT changed": the marketing,
service and back-office kits. Three further sites carry service-tier vocabulary outside the lexicon
section (a type-scale description, an icon-name list, and the back-office kit's own description) and
should be left alone for the same reason.

## Deviations from Plan

### Auto-fixed issues

**1. [Rule 1 — Bug] The glyph import extractor matched across adjacent imports**
- **Found during:** Task 1, first run
- **Issue:** The lazy `{[\s\S]*?}` specifier pattern let one match START at an earlier import's
  brace and END at the icon package's, swallowing every binding between. `components/ui/sonner.tsx`
  opens `import { Toaster as Sonner } from "sonner"`, so `Sonner` was attributed to the icon package
  and the file's own `<Sonner />` was reported as an unmigrated glyph.
- **Why it matters:** the "fix" this false positive invites is wrapping a component that is not a
  glyph at all.
- **Fix:** brace-excluding character class (`{[^{}]*}`), so a match cannot span two imports.
- **Commit:** `7d0c25a`

**2. [Rule 1 — Bug] The prose-tally cross-check matched nothing because the tally is line-wrapped**
- **Found during:** Task 1, first run
- **Issue:** space-literal pattern against a tally that wraps mid-phrase in the source. The assertion
  did not fail loudly — it simply matched `null`, which is the silent-green failure mode the whole
  file exists to prevent.
- **Fix:** `\s+` throughout both prose patterns.
- **Commit:** `7d0c25a`

**3. [Rule 3 — Blocking] `tsc` rejected the direct cast on the copy deck**
- **Issue:** `DINER_COPY` is not uniformly `Record<string, Record<string, string>>` — `emptyFilter`
  nests a heading and a body — so the direct assertion did not typecheck.
- **Fix:** routed through `unknown` with a comment recording *why* the probe is structural: a typed
  access would stop compiling the moment a key were deleted, converting the defect this group reports
  into a broken build with no diagnostic.
- **Commit:** `7d0c25a`

### Deliberate divergence from an acceptance criterion

**Group 3's per-row owner assertion is conditional on the verdict, not unconditional.** The plan's
criterion reads "every row carries both a verdict and an owning phase". Ten of the eleven rows are
`partial` and every one names a phase. The eleventh (`DINE-05`) is the single `HOLDS` row: it owes no
residue, so it names nobody. Asserting unconditionally would have forced inventing an owner for a
debt that does not exist — the test would have been made green by editing the document, which is
precisely the failure this group guards.

Compensated with two checks that are strictly stronger than the one dropped: set-equality against the
eleven IDs (catches an invented row as well as a lost one), and a cross-check of the table's
holds/partial counts against the prose tally above it (catches an edit to either record that skips
the other). The dropped-row rehearsal below shows all three firing together.

## The four RED observations (acceptance criterion 5)

Each group was made to fail against a deliberate violation, the message recorded, and the violation
reverted with `git checkout -- <file>`.

**Group 1 — bare glyph.** Replaced the wrapper call in `components/ui/checkbox.tsx` with a direct
render:

> UNMIGRATED GLYPH — components/ui/checkbox.tsx renders CheckIcon directly as a JSX element, so it
> draws at Lucide's stock stroke of 2 instead of the design system's 1.75. Route it through the
> wrapper instead: `<Icon icon={CheckIcon} />` (components/ui/icon.tsx, plan 01.1-07). This is the
> last unmigrated call site of a nineteen-file migration spread across five plans.

**Group 2 — ramp identifier on a surface.** Appended a numeric step to a family word already present
as prose in `components/ui/tag.tsx`:

> RAW RAMP IDENTIFIER ON A SURFACE — components/ui/tag.tsx: napfeny-200. Only app/tokens/cena.css may
> write the ramp's own step names; every other file must consume a semantic token (--cena-ink,
> --cena-accent, --cena-warning-soft …). A raw ramp name is un-themable BY CONSTRUCTION — no theme
> can re-map a name it does not own — and that is a structural requirement, not a brand one, so it
> holds even though v1 ships exactly one brand (revised D-02).

*(This rehearsal doubles as proof the family-word/step distinction works: the word was already in
that comment and green; adding the step turned it red.)*

**Group 3 — deleted residue row.** Removed the `MENU-10` row. Three assertions fired:

> Only 10 rows parsed out of 01.1-UI-SPEC.md § "What the template does NOT cover" … expected 10 to be
> greater than or equal to 11

> The residue table no longer matches the eleven requirement IDs the imported diner template
> self-declares. A LOST ROW IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A MET REQUIREMENT: the residue simply stops
> being owed by anybody, and a README's self-report becomes settled fact (D-05).

> The table now carries 1 holds and 9 partial rows, but the prose above it claims 1 and 10. One of
> the two was edited without the other.

**Group 4 — removed language key.** Emptied the Romanian allergen disclaimer:

> INCOMPLETE VOCABULARY — `allergenDisclaimer` (the allergen disclaimer (DINE-06)) is missing or empty
> for: ro. The diner menu ships hu/en/ro; a group present in only some of them is a surface that falls
> back to a language the diner did not choose.

## Carried-forward findings — disposition

**1. `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` contradicts itself on the mono family. OPEN — confirmed, and it will bite
Phase 2.** Line 148 (§ "Family axis"): `--font-mono` "renders at the Label or Body role, never at a
size of its own." Lines 608 and 866: "Prices render in `--font-mono` at the Heading role." A price is
the single most common mono string in the product, so the two rules collide on the default case, not
an edge. Plan 01.1-12 followed the Body reading for PIN digits — which is consistent with line 148
and with a PIN not being a price. **Recommendation:** resolve in favour of the *Currency* section
(price at Heading) and narrow line 148 to "Label or Body **except prices**", because the price rule is
stated twice, is tied to a specific measured layout, and is what the diner row and item sheet both
depend on. Owner: the phase that ships the diner price display (Phase 2, DINE-01). Do not let that
phase resolve it by picking whichever it reads first.

**2. Nine tablet-route-group strings have no `lib/copy.ts` contract row. OPEN — confirmed.** Verified
present in source and absent from the contract: `"Manage this venue"`
(`app/(tablet)/unlock/page.tsx:75`), `"Setting up…"` (`EnableStaffModeForm.tsx:107`), `"Locking…"`
(`ExitOwnerModeButton.tsx:41`), the delete-key `aria-label` (`NameGridPinPad.tsx:321`), and five more.
The copy tripwire only catches *deck* strings missing a row, so these are structurally invisible to
it. Plans 01.1-12 and 01.1-13 both declined to add them because their wave's acceptance demanded an
empty `lib/copy.ts` diff — a correct call at the time, and the reason the debt is still open.
**Recommendation:** a small dedicated plan that adds the rows *and* widens the tripwire to scan
rendered strings in the tablet route group, since adding rows without widening the tripwire leaves
the next nine equally invisible. Owner: a Phase 2 side plan or a phase-01 cleanup.

**3. `01.1-PATTERNS.md` is factually wrong about `components/dashboard-nav.tsx`. OPEN — confirmed,
and it was wrong from the start.** Line 389 asserts that file "and `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` are
Server Components today and must stay so." The layout half is correct. `dashboard-nav.tsx` has
carried the client directive since Phase 01's first commit (`0dddf5e`) because it reads
`usePathname()`; it could never have been a Server Component. Plan 01.1-10 documented the
discrepancy rather than breaking the build to satisfy it — the right call. **Recommendation:** strike
`components/dashboard-nav.tsx` from that sentence. It is a one-line correction to a phase document,
but it is load-bearing: a later agent that trusts it will try to remove a directive the file needs and
will get a runtime error it then has to diagnose.

**4. `.design-sync/` is stale after the typeface change. RESOLVED (recorded).** Task 3 wrote the full
record into `.design-sync/NOTES.md`: three named artifacts, each with its consequence; the
screenshots' expected-to-change status; and the D-12 deferral marked ready-to-decide without
deciding it. Already tracked in `.planning/WINDOWS.md`. Verified the specifics rather than repeating
the claim: `.design-sync/fonts/` holds only Inter; `tailwind-entry.css`'s `:root` defines
`--font-sans` as Inter and declares no `--font-serif`/`--font-mono` at all; its safelists enumerate
the shadcn semantic roles only, so 01.1's new token vocabulary is invisible to the preview; and
`config.json`'s `projectId` (`25b3418f-…`) is not the project 01.1 works against (`07b799d4-…`).

**5. `01-UAT.md`'s "Owed: six rows" was wrong (real figure 40). CLOSED by plan 01.1-13** against the
correct figure. No action here; recorded so the correction is not re-litigated.
